title: MSAA 3D is 4×
evidence: msaa_3d is 2. The hint is Disabled, 2×, 4×, 8×, so 2 is 4×. The antialiasing page says higher levels are significantly more demanding.
suggestion: Try 2× (value 1) or TAA (Forward+ only) if 4× shows up in the frame time.
tradeoff: 2× leaves more edge aliasing than 4×. TAA adds blur and ghosting.
expected_effect: Fewer coverage samples. Compare frame_timing.

title: MSAA 3D is 8×
evidence: msaa_3d is 3 (8×). The antialiasing page says 8× MSAA is usually too demanding and recommends staying at 2× or 4× for modern visuals.
suggestion: Set rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/msaa_3d to 2 (4×) or 1 (2×).
tradeoff: Edges alias more than at 8×.
expected_effect: A large drop in MSAA sample cost, as characterized on the antialiasing page, still to be measured in this project.

title: MSAA 3D is on with the Mobile renderer
evidence: Mobile renderer with msaa_3d above 0. The antialiasing page says that on mobile, FXAA is usually the viable option and higher MSAA levels are unlikely to run smoothly.
suggestion: Set msaa_3d to 0 and set screen_space_aa to 1 (FXAA), which the page says is available on Mobile.
tradeoff: FXAA is blurrier than MSAA and does little for specular aliasing.
expected_effect: Replaces MSAA with the low-cost post pass the page recommends for low-end GPUs.

title: MSAA and TAA are both enabled
heuristic_rationale: The antialiasing page says stacking techniques is usually unnecessary. It does not forbid the combination.
evidence: msaa_3d is above 0 and use_taa is true. TAA is Forward+ only.
suggestion: Keep one of them. The page says TAA is the usual choice against specular aliasing, and MSAA can be added only when there is spare GPU time.
tradeoff: Dropping MSAA leaves more geometric aliasing. Dropping TAA leaves more specular shimmer and adds no blur.
expected_effect: One less full antialiasing technique. Measure both ways.

title: TAA is enabled
evidence: use_taa is true and FSR 2.2 is not the scaling mode. The page says TAA has a medium cost, blurs in motion, and ghosts.
suggestion: Turn use_taa off and compare. If FSR 2.2 is enabled later, this setting is ignored because FSR 2.2 supplies temporal antialiasing.
tradeoff: Specular and edge shimmer return.
expected_effect: Removes the TAA pass. Read the TAA timestamp when it is present.

title: FXAA is the screen-space antialiasing mode
evidence: screen_space_aa is 1. On 4.4 the hint is Disabled, FXAA. On 4.7 it is Disabled, FXAA, SMAA, so 1 is still FXAA. The page calls FXAA the fastest antialiasing method and a moderate blur.
suggestion: Leave FXAA if the GPU is tight. On Forward+ with headroom, TAA covers specular aliasing better.
tradeoff: TAA costs more and ghosts. Disabling FXAA exposes edges.
expected_effect: FXAA is a cheap fullscreen pass. Confirm with frame_timing rather than a fixed millisecond cost.

title: No 3D antialiasing is enabled
evidence: msaa_3d, use_taa, and screen_space_aa are off, scale is not above 1, and mode is not FSR 2.2. The antialiasing page treats that combination as no edge antialiasing.
suggestion: With GPU headroom: Forward+ can enable use_taa. Mobile can set screen_space_aa to 1 (FXAA). Compatibility can use msaa_3d 1 (2×). This is optional.
tradeoff: Every method on the page costs GPU time or adds blur.
expected_effect: Smoother edges. Measure before shipping it.

title: Screen-space roughness limiter is off
evidence: The limiter is disabled. The antialiasing page says it is on by default, has a small performance impact, and reduces specular aliasing.
suggestion: Set rendering/anti_aliasing/screen_space_roughness_limiter/enabled to true. Defaults are amount 0.25 and limit 0.18.
tradeoff: A small extra cost, which the page says to skip only when specular aliasing is not a problem.
expected_effect: Less specular shimmer on detailed geometry. Not an edge antialiasing method.

title: Debanding is enabled
evidence: rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/use_debanding is true. The default is false.
suggestion: Turn use_debanding off and check gradients. It is an extra fullscreen operation on top of the default off state.
tradeoff: Color banding can show in gradients and fog.
expected_effect: One less fullscreen step. Measure; the class reference does not publish a millisecond cost.

title: 2D MSAA is 4× or 8×
evidence: msaa_2d is 2 or 3 (4× or 8×). The hint matches 3D: Disabled, 2×, 4×, 8×. The default is 0.
suggestion: Set rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/msaa_2d to 0 or 1 unless 2D edges need the higher sample count.
tradeoff: 2D edges alias more.
expected_effect: Fewer 2D coverage samples. This setting is independent of msaa_3d.

title: TAA is in the capture
heuristic_rationale: The trigger is a RenderingDevice timestamp label substring from Godot's clustered renderer. Labels are not a stable public API. The rule fires only when that pass has exclusive time above 0.
evidence: The TAA timestamp is present. TAA is Forward+ only and has a medium cost on the antialiasing page.
suggestion: Turn use_taa off if another antialiasing method is enough.
tradeoff: Turning the feature off changes the look described on the cited page.
expected_effect: That pass should shrink or disappear on the next gpu_passes capture. No percentage is predicted.

title: SMAA is the screen-space antialiasing mode
evidence: Sets the screen-space antialiasing mode
suggestion: Viewport.SCREEN_SPACE_AA_SMAA is 2 in Godot 4.7. Set rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/screen_space_aa to 0 or to FXAA if you need the post pass gone or cheaper.
tradeoff: Edges are aliased if you also leave MSAA off.
expected_effect: Re-measure with collect_metrics after changing this setting. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

title: SMAA edge detection is more sensitive than the default
evidence: Lower values will catch more edges, at a potentially higher performance cost
suggestion: Raise rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/smaa_edge_detection_threshold toward 0.05. The description says lower values cost more.
tradeoff: Faint edges are no longer smoothed.
expected_effect: Re-measure with collect_metrics after changing this setting. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

title: A SubViewport combines MSAA with FXAA
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An update-enabled 3D SubViewport enables both MSAA and FXAA. The native RD post-process selects FXAA independently of the MSAA setting; their costs can combine. The methods target different aliasing, so combining them is not automatically wrong.
suggestion: Compare each method on its own in this viewport, measuring GPU time and inspecting both geometry edges and specular shimmer.
tradeoff: Removing MSAA can worsen geometric edges; removing FXAA can expose shader aliasing. FXAA can also soften fine detail.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: A SubViewport uses 4x or 8x 2D MSAA
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An update-enabled SubViewport has msaa_2d set to 4x or 8x. Its canvas sample count is independent of the root viewport's project setting. Disabled viewport updates are excluded.
suggestion: Compare 2x MSAA or disabled MSAA for this viewport's 2D content.
tradeoff: Canvas geometry edges may alias more; MSAA does not fix texture or shader aliasing.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: TAA is enabled together with a temporal upscaler
evidence: Godot prints "FSR 2 or MetalFX Temporal is not compatible with TAA. Disabling TAA internally." when use_taa is on and the scaling mode is FSR 2.2 (2) or MetalFX Temporal (4). The upscaler provides its own temporal antialiasing and Godot turns TAA off.
suggestion: Turn rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/use_taa off; the temporal upscaler already antialiases.
tradeoff: None; TAA is already disabled while the temporal upscaler runs.
expected_effect: Godot uses the configuration as written instead of overriding or ignoring it; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: audit_project_rendering or scan_scene, then run the game and confirm the warning is gone from the output

title: TAA is enabled outside Forward+
evidence: Godot prints "TAA is only available when using the Forward+ renderer." when use_taa is on under the Mobile or Compatibility renderer, which have no TAA pass.
suggestion: Turn use_taa off for this renderer and choose another antialiasing method (MSAA or FXAA where available).
tradeoff: Without TAA, specular and geometric aliasing remain unless another method is enabled.
expected_effect: Godot uses the configuration as written instead of overriding or ignoring it; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: audit_project_rendering or scan_scene, then run the game and confirm the warning is gone from the output

title: Screen-space antialiasing is set under Compatibility
evidence: Godot prints "Screen-space AA is only available when using the Forward+ or Mobile renderer." when screen_space_aa is FXAA or SMAA under the Compatibility renderer, which does not run it.
suggestion: Set screen_space_aa to Disabled and use MSAA under Compatibility.
tradeoff: MSAA does not smooth shader or transparency aliasing.
expected_effect: Godot uses the configuration as written instead of overriding or ignoring it; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: audit_project_rendering or scan_scene, then run the game and confirm the warning is gone from the output

title: 2D MSAA is set under Compatibility
evidence: Godot prints "2D MSAA is not yet supported for GLES3." when msaa_2d is above Disabled under the Compatibility renderer, so 2D content is not multisampled.
suggestion: Set msaa_2d to Disabled, or antialias 2D lines and polygons with their antialiased properties.
tradeoff: Polygon and line edges stay aliased unless drawn antialiased.
expected_effect: Godot uses the configuration as written instead of overriding or ignoring it; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: audit_project_rendering or scan_scene, then run the game and confirm the warning is gone from the output

title: MetalFX Temporal upscaling is combined with 3D MSAA
evidence: Godot prints "MetalFX temporal upscaling does not support 3D MSAA. Disabling 3D MSAA internally." on Apple devices that run MetalFX Temporal (scaling mode 4) when msaa_3d is enabled; MSAA is turned off while the upscaler runs.
suggestion: Set msaa_3d to Disabled when using MetalFX Temporal, or choose another scaling mode.
tradeoff: None on devices that run MetalFX Temporal; other devices fall back to another upscaler and keep MSAA.
expected_effect: Godot uses the configuration as written instead of overriding or ignoring it; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: audit_project_rendering or scan_scene, then run the game and confirm the warning is gone from the output
